cases.title: Dataclass field input
cases.quote:
* When used as fields, dataclasses (Pydantic or vanilla) no longer accept tuples as validation inputs; dicts should be
  used instead.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, can a dataclass used as a model field be populated from a tuple, or should I supply a dictionary?
cases.answer: Supply a dictionary; Pydantic and vanilla dataclasses used as fields no longer accept tuple validation inputs.
cases.rubric: Reject tuple acceptance for the stated field context; do not claim dataclass instances or every possible input type are forbidden.

cases.title: Dataclass initialization hook
cases.quote: * The `__post_init__` in Pydantic dataclasses will now be called _after_ validation, rather than before.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, does a Pydantic dataclass's __post_init__ run before or after validation?
cases.rubric: Require the temporal order after validation; distinguish Pydantic dataclasses from a universal statement about Python dataclasses.

cases.title: Dataclass extra inputs
cases.quote:
* Pydantic no longer supports `extra='allow'` for Pydantic dataclasses, where extra fields passed to the initializer would be
    stored as extra attributes on the dataclass. `extra='ignore'` is still supported for the purpose of ignoring
    unexpected fields while parsing data, they just won't be stored on the instance.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, can extra='allow' store unexpected initializer fields on a Pydantic dataclass? What does extra='ignore' do?
cases.answer: Storing extras with extra='allow' is unsupported for Pydantic dataclasses. extra='ignore' discards unexpected fields rather than storing them.
cases.rubric: Require both the unsupported storage behavior and ignore/discard distinction; do not generalize to BaseModel extra handling.

cases.title: Vanilla dataclass configuration
cases.quote:
* In Pydantic V1, if you used a vanilla (i.e., non-Pydantic) dataclass as a field, the config of the parent type would
    be used as though it was the config for the dataclass itself as well. In Pydantic V2, this is no longer the case.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, does a vanilla dataclass used as a field inherit the parent model's configuration, and how can its configuration be overridden?
cases.answer: It does not inherit the parent model's configuration. Use the config parameter of the dataclass decorator to override configuration.
cases.rubric: Reject automatic propagation of the parent config; require the decorator config parameter, not an invented __pydantic_model__ setting.

cases.title: Model configuration representation
cases.quote:
* In Pydantic V2, to specify config on a model, you should set a class attribute called `model_config` to be a dict
  with the key/value pairs you want to be used as the config. The Pydantic V1 behavior to create a class called `Config`
  in the namespace of the parent `BaseModel` subclass is now deprecated.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, what is the recommended way to declare model configuration, and is the inner Config class recommended?
cases.answer: Declare a model_config class attribute containing a dictionary of settings. The inner Config class approach is deprecated.
cases.rubric: Distinguish deprecated from removed; require model_config rather than a configuration field on each model instance.

cases.title: Configuration inheritance precedence
cases.quote: will be merged, and for any settings defined in both, those from `Model2` will override those from `Model1`.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, for class MyModel(Model1, Model2), how are non-default model_config settings combined when both parents define the same setting?
cases.answer: The non-default settings are merged; Model2 overrides Model1 for settings defined in both.
cases.rubric: Require the right-hand Model2 precedence in this explicitly described inheritance order; reject left-parent-wins or replacing all settings wholesale.

cases.title: Native v2 generic model declaration
cases.quote: create generic `BaseModel` subclasses by just adding `Generic` as a parent class on a `BaseModel` subclass directly.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6's native v2 API, how should I declare a generic model without pydantic.generics.GenericModel?
cases.answer: Inherit from BaseModel and typing.Generic[T], for example class MyModel(BaseModel, Generic[T]). GenericModel is no longer necessary.
cases.rubric: Require both BaseModel and Generic[T]; do not confuse this declaration rule with runtime TypeVar bound checking or recommend mixing v1 model parameters into a v2 generic.

cases.title: Mapping subtype preservation
cases.end: ### Changes to Handling of Standard Types
cases.quote:
In Pydantic V2 we no longer attempt to preserve the input type in all cases; instead, we only promise that the output
type will match the type annotations.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, if I validate a Counter as Mapping[str, int], is preserving the Counter subtype guaranteed?
cases.answer: No. Pydantic guarantees output matching the annotation, not preservation of every input subtype; the documented Mapping example produces a plain dict.
cases.rubric: Reject a guarantee of Counter preservation; do not claim every type always loses its subtype, because the guide notes preservation exceptions.

cases.title: URL values and string APIs
cases.start: ### Url and Dsn types in `pydantic.networks` no longer inherit from `str`
cases.quote: types in APIs which expect `str` you'll now need to convert them (with `str(url)`).
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, do URL and DSN values inherit from str, and how should I pass a URL value to an API expecting a string?
cases.answer: They no longer inherit from str; explicitly convert the value with str(url).
cases.rubric: Require both the inheritance distinction and explicit conversion; do not claim the URL value cannot be represented as a string.
